subject: Enhance BUML model generation and fix multiple issues
message:
Enhance BUML model generation and fix multiple issues

Association & Enumeration Improvements:
- Improve association naming using class names instead of labels
- Add support for both HTML-encoded (<<) and regular chevrons (>>) for enumeration detection
- Add enumeration type linking with class attributes
- Make association label position detection more flexible
- Add visibility support for association ends (public/private)
- Support multiple labels per edge (name and multiplicity)
- Fix double detection of enumerations in XML parsing

Method & Parameter Handling:
- Fix method generation by removing return_type reference
- Update method parameter handling to support default values
- Improve parameter extraction and formatting
- Clean up method visibility handling

Enumeration Literal Fixes:
- Fix enumeration literal handling to prevent double encapsulation
- Correct enumeration literal extraction with proper visibility markers
- Update save_buml_to_file to handle enumeration types correctly
- Fix EnumerationLiteral object creation and attribute access

Technical Improvements:
- Update XML parsing logic for better robustness
- Improve class attribute type detection and linking
- Enhance multiplicity parsing for association ends
- Clean up attribute and method extraction logic
- Add proper error handling for XML parsing
- Ensure consistent formatting in generated BUML model file

v4.2.0 (#329)

# Version 4.2.0

## New Features and Improvements

### Web Modeling Editor

- Introduced association popup component for enhanced object linking functionality, enabling users to connect objects to related classes in both standard and icon object diagrams.
- Added an icon attribute to class metadata, allowing classes to store an icon that is displayed for instantiated objects in object diagrams.
- Improved UI consistency and maintainability with reformatted HTML elements, better input attributes, button layouts, and section structure.
- Enhanced palette and preview support for the new diagram types in the create pane interface.

### BESSER Low-code Platform

- Added new FastAPI endpoint `/besser_api/get-json-model-from-image` that accepts an image and OpenAI API key to convert UML images to JSON models using the `image_to_buml` functionality.
- Enhanced Smart Data Models JSON schema generator with improvements for better compatibility and validation rules.
- Extended metadata handling in code builder, BUML-to-JSON converter, and JSON-to-BUML processor to include `icon` field support.
- Updated `image_to_buml` prompt to clarify handling of association labels for better PlantUML compatibility.

* Add Action classes and enhance Body composition

Introduces the Action base class and its derivatives (CustomCodeAction, ReplyAction) to enable modular composition of state machine bodies. This refactor allows more flexible and extensible modeling of state machine behaviors.

* Update agent_mm.png diagram

Replaces the agent_mm.png image in documentation with a new version. Ensures the diagram reflects the latest changes or improvements.

* Refactor agent body handling to use ReplyAction

Agent body and fallback body message handling now uses ReplyAction objects instead of direct reply calls. This change improves consistency in agent code generation and processing, and updates template, code builder, and JSON-to-BUML converter logic to support the new action-based approach.

* Handle ReplyAction bodies in agent diagram converter

Adds logic to detect and process ReplyAction actions when converting agent diagrams, ensuring that set_body and set_fallback_body correctly handle bodies associated with ReplyAction. This improves support for text reply bodies in the generated JSON output.

Introduces the LLMReply action to support AI-generated responses in agent state machines. message:
v6.0.0

# Version 6.0.0

This release introduces **GitHub OAuth integration and automatic deployment on Render**,  
along with improved environment configuration, frontend flexibility across environments, and important backend code-generation fixes.

## New Features

### GitHub OAuth Integration & Render Auto-Deployment

- Added **GitHub OAuth integration for WME**, enabling secure authentication and repository authorization.
- Implemented a **deployment API that automatically provisions and deploys applications on Render** after successful OAuth authentication.
- Deployment flow eliminates manual setup by linking GitHub repositories directly to Render services.

## Improvements

- Added a comprehensive `.env.example` file documenting all required environment variables.
- Replaced hardcoded backend URLs in generated React components with `process.env.REACT_APP_API_URL`, enabling flexible frontend deployment across environments.

## Bug Fixes

- #378 
### Backend Code Generation: 
- Refactored object creation logic to use **Jinja2 namespaces** for collecting constructor arguments, fixing issues with missing or duplicated parameters.
- Improved generated REST endpoints for **many-to-many (N:M) relationships**, including self-referential associations, to avoid naming conflicts and ensure correct query generation.

- Updated `BarChart`, `LineChart`, `PieChart`, `RadarChart`, and `RadialBarChart` to transform data structures for compatibility with Recharts when using nested fields.
- Modified data fetching logic in the renderer to append `?detailed=true` for API requests involving nested fields.
- Improved series color handling by extracting color attributes from series configurations and ensuring they are preserved in generated code.
- Added support for series filters in all chart parsers, allowing filter expressions to be passed to the `DataBinding` object.
- Fixed GUI diagram code generation issues, enabling successful web application generation from the graphical UI editor.
- Cleaned up JSON output by removing redundant data and ensuring only necessary serialized data is included.

BREAKING CHANGE: Existing charts using complex models can now simplify data bindings to use dot notation directly.

subject: fix: resolve agent restart loop on Render deployment (#442)
message:
fix: resolve agent restart loop on Render deployment (#442)

The agent service deployment on Render was stuck in a restart loop due to
three issues in the generated render.yaml configuration:

1. NLTK data resources were downloaded at runtime on every startup instead
   of being cached during the build phase, causing slow starts and timeouts
2. The agent's WebSocket server was bound to localhost:8765 instead of
   0.0.0.0:$PORT, so Render's health checks could never reach it
3. The OpenAI API key was not injected from environment variables into the
   agent's config.ini

Changes to the agent service in render.yaml:
- Build command now downloads NLTK data ('popular') during the build phase
- Start command configures config.ini via sed to bind to 0.0.0.0 on
  Render's assigned $PORT and inject $OPENAI_API_KEY before launching
- Removed hardcoded PORT=8765 env var (Render assigns its own PORT)
- Added OPENAI_API_KEY env var with sync:false for manual configuration

message:
fix: agent config fallback + Render port binding for streamlit

Two fixes:

1. Agent config not reaching BAFGenerator in webapp flow:
   The frontend may store the agent config at the project settings
   level rather than on the individual AgentDiagram. Added fallback
   chain: diagram-level config -> project-level settings config.
   This ensures LLM instantiation, intent recognition, and platform
   settings are properly rendered in the generated agent code.

2. Render "no open ports" timeout:
   use_ui=True starts both WebSocket and Streamlit servers.
   The start command only patched websocket.host/port but left
   streamlit.host=localhost and streamlit.port=5000 untouched.
   Render's health check couldn't reach either server. Now both
   websocket and streamlit host/port are rewritten to 0.0.0.0:$PORT.

subject: fix: config fallback chain + default LLM-based intent classifier
message:
fix: config fallback chain + default LLM-based intent classifier

Two fixes for the agent crash on Render deployment:

1. Config fallback chain: When generating an agent as part of a webapp
   project, the AgentDiagram's config field may be empty if the
   frontend stores it at the project settings level instead. Added
   fallback: try diagram-level config -> project-level settings config.
   This ensures LLM settings and intent recognition technology are
   passed to the BAF generator.

2. Default to LLM-based intent classification: When no intent
   classifier configuration is provided (neither from config nor from
   agent model), BAF defaults to SimpleIntentClassifier which requires
   PyTorch. Since PyTorch is a heavy dependency (200MB+) not included
   in standard installs, the agent crashes with:
   NameError: name 'nn' is not defined
   Now the template falls back to LLMIntentClassifierConfiguration
   (using gpt-4o-mini) which only needs an API key. This prevents
   the crash and is a reasonable default for deployed agents.

fix: remove streamlit port override to avoid port conflict on Render

Setting both websocket.port and streamlit.port to $PORT would cause a
port conflict since both servers try to bind the same port. The WebSocket
server is the one that needs $PORT (it's what the Next.js frontend
connects to). Streamlit can use its default port (5000) internally since
it's not externally exposed in the deployment architecture.

subject: fix(tests): stop nn conftest from leaking MagicMock into sys.modules
message:
fix(tests): stop nn conftest from leaking MagicMock into sys.modules

The NN converter conftest used sys.modules.setdefault() to stub out
bocl, yaml, docker, github and openai. Because pytest imports every
conftest.py during collection — before any test has had a chance to
import the real packages — the MagicMock stubs landed in the global
import cache first. Later tests that did `from bocl.OCLWrapper import
OCLWrapper` (e.g. tests/BUML/metamodel/ocl/test_comprehensive_constraints.py)
then received the MagicMock instead of the real class, and every
constraint assertion failed with
    assert <MagicMock name='mock.OCLWrapper().evaluate()'> is True

Now each optional module is only replaced with a MagicMock if the real
package genuinely cannot be imported. In CI (where bocl==1.0.0 is
installed via backend/requirements.txt) the real module is loaded and
no global pollution occurs; in a minimal local env the fallback still
works.

subject: fix: pin standalone agent generation to request temp dir
message:
fix: pin standalone agent generation to request temp dir

_handle_agent_generation created BAFGenerator without passing
output_dir, so GeneratorInterface.build_generation_dir() fell back to
<CWD>/output. Two problems:

1. The downstream zip harvester in generate_agent_files walks
   os.path.join(temp_dir, OUTPUT_DIR_NAME), which is a completely
   different path. The for-loop silently skipped because the directory
   doesn't exist, and the final agent_output.zip ended up containing
   only agent_model.py (the raw BUML source) with none of the actual
   BAFGenerator output (<agent_name>.py, config.yaml, readme.txt, RAG
   subdirs). The WebApp-embedded agent flow worked because
   web_app_generator.py:124 passes output_dir=agent_dir explicitly.

2. Concurrent requests polluted each other via the shared
   <CWD>/output folder, and leftover files leaked into later
   downloads.

Pin both BAFGenerator constructor branches to
os.path.join(temp_dir, OUTPUT_DIR_NAME) so the generator writes
exactly where the harvester looks. The existing tempfile cleanup now
also cleans up the generator output automatically.

subject: fix: more permissive PlantUML importer syntax (closes #236)
message:
fix: more permissive PlantUML importer syntax (closes #236)

The PlantUML-to-BUML importer was rejecting three syntaxes that
PlantUML itself accepts, forcing users to rewrite their models before
importing:

1. Single-dash `-` as an association edge (used by PlantUML for
   horizontal layout). The grammar hardcoded `'--'` in every
   association rule (bidirectional, unidirectional, aggregation,
   composition) and failed to parse `Source - Target`. Grammar now
   accepts `('--' | '-')` in all four rules. Longest-match in the
   lexer keeps `--` associations working unchanged.
2. Primitive type aliases. The grammar accepted `string` but not
   `integer` or `boolean`, and the listener only mapped `string -> str`.
   Grammar now also accepts `integer` and `boolean`; the listener maps
   `{string -> str, integer -> int, boolean -> bool}` via a lookup so
   all three resolve to the same singleton as their short form.
3. Trailing direction hint `<`/`>` after an association label
   (e.g. `A - B : rel >`). The grammar rejected it as "extraneous
   input"; it's a rendering hint in PlantUML with no semantic meaning.
   Grammar now accepts and discards it.

The multiplicity `*` case from the issue already worked — the listener
passes `"*"` to the `Multiplicity` constructor, which stores it as
`UNLIMITED_MAX_MULTIPLICITY` (9999) per the project-wide convention
documented in CLAUDE.md. Changing that would sweep across every
generator and isn't in scope for the importer fix.

Regenerated lexer/parser/listener with ANTLR 4.13.2 from the updated
`.g4`. Added 5 regression tests in
`tests/BUML/notations/structuralPlantUML/test_permissive_syntax.py`
covering the full repro from the issue, the type aliases, the
`<`/`>` hint, and a guard that `--` still parses. All 14 tests in the
suite (5 new + 9 pre-existing) pass.

message:
feat: add is_external_id property end-to-end

Introduces a new Property.is_external_id flag — a user-facing identifier
distinct from the internal/surrogate primary key (is_id). Per
@he5ffedc37ea59c4c's guidance on #108, the framing pivots from "define unique
primary keys" to "define external ids", which #230 proposes as a
first-class metamodel concept and #225 illustrates as the concrete
Django pain point (ForeignKey dropdowns showing the PK number instead
of a meaningful label).

Closes #230.
Closes #225.
Closes #108.

Metamodel (besser/BUML/metamodel/structural/structural.py):
- Property.is_external_id: bool = False with a setter that rejects
  is_external_id=True when the property is already optional, and an
  is_optional setter that rejects is_optional=True on an existing
  external identifier (same pattern as the is_id <-> is_optional
  constraint). is_id and is_external_id may coexist when a natural
  key also serves as the PK (e.g. isbn).

JSON <-> BUML converters:
- class_diagram_processor.py (json_to_buml): parse the isExternalId
  key from the diagram JSON.
- class_diagram_converter.py (buml_to_json): emit isExternalId in
  the generated JSON, keeping the round-trip symmetric with isId
  and isOptional.

BUML code builder (besser/utilities/buml_code_builder/domain_model_builder.py):
- Emit is_external_id=True in the generated Property() for both
  regular class attributes and association class attributes so that
  exporting a model to Python and re-executing the file preserves
  the flag.

SQLAlchemy generator:
- helpers.py.j2 and sql_alchemy_template.py.j2 now emit
  `unique=True` on mapped columns when the attribute is marked
  is_external_id=True and is not the primary key. This addresses
  #108's UNIQUE-attribute ask transitively without introducing a
  separate is_unique flag. The SQL generator inherits the UNIQUE
  constraint via the SQLAlchemy wrapper.

Django generator:
- django_fields.py.j2: emit `primary_key=True` for is_id and
  `unique=True` for is_external_id (non-PK) on every field type.
- models.py.j2: __str__ prefers is_external_id attributes,
  composing them with " - ".join(...) when multiple are declared.
  Falls back to the first primitive attribute by timestamp when
  no external id is set, preserving existing behavior. This is
  what fixes #225 — Django admin dropdowns and {{ object }}
  renderings now show the meaningful label.
- models.py.j2: fixed a pre-existing whitespace bug where the
  {%- for attr %} ... {%- endfor %} block was stripping every
  newline, collapsing all attribute assignments onto the same
  line as the class docstring and producing invalid Python. The
  old Django tests only compared strings so it went unnoticed;
  the new test_rendered_models_are_valid_python guards against it.

Frontend (besser/utilities/web_modeling_editor/frontend -> b5102c0):
- Adds an "External ID" checkbox to the attribute style pane,
  symmetric with the ID checkbox. Display name shows trailing
  {external id} (or {id, external id}) markers. Toggling either
  flag forces isOptional off to respect the metamodel constraint.

Tests (11 new):
- Metamodel: test_property_is_external_id_validation covers default,
  init, coexistence with is_id, and all three setter-conflict paths.
- Converter round-trip: test_attribute_is_id_and_external_id_preserved
  mutates the fixture and asserts both flags survive JSON -> BUML -> JSON.
- Code builder: test_is_external_id_roundtrip writes, exec's, and
  asserts the flag survives; plus the earlier test_is_id_roundtrip
  retained.
- SQLAlchemy: test_is_external_id.py (3 tests) verifies
  * the UNIQUE constraint appears via sqlalchemy.inspect
  * inserting duplicate external-id values actually raises
    IntegrityError against an in-memory engine
  * is_id on a non-"id"-named attribute becomes the real PK
- Django: test_is_id_external_id.py (6 tests) verifies
  primary_key / unique emission, __str__ using single / composite /
  fallback external ids, and that the rendered models.py compiles
  as valid Python.

Generators intentionally left alone: Pydantic and JSON Schema have
no PK concept; REST/FastAPI would need a URL-lookup design call;
React / Flutter / Python-class / Java-class could benefit from

subject: fix: OCL accepts attributes named `size` (closes #198)
message:
fix: OCL accepts attributes named `size` (closes #198)

`size` is a reserved lexer keyword for the OCL `->size()` / `.size()`
collection operation, so the lexer always tokenized a class attribute
named `size` as the `SIZE` token rather than a generic `ID`. The
`dotNavigation` rule matches only `ID`, so any domain model with a
`size` attribute failed to parse with
`mismatched input '>' expecting '('` — the parser fell through to
looking for the `.size()` call form and expected `LPAREN` to follow.

Issue #198 blamed inheritance because Jordi's example had `size` on a
parent class (`Unit`) inherited by `Department`, but the bug fires
identically on a *direct* attribute — the keyword collision is the
real trigger, not the inheritance resolver (which already uses
`Class.all_attributes()` correctly).

Grammar fix: add `expression DOT SIZE #dotSizeNavigation` as a
fallback rule below the existing `DOT SIZE LPAREN RPAREN #dotSize`.
ANTLR's longest-match keeps the `.size()` method-call form winning
when parens follow, so `collection->size()` and `string.size()` still
parse unchanged; only the no-parens case now also matches.

Visitor: new `visitDotSizeNavigation` that resolves `size` via the
same `_resolve_property` / `_resolve_property_in_iterators` path as
`visitDotNavigation`, hardcoding the name `"size"`.

Regenerated the lexer, parser, and visitor base class with
ANTLR 4.13.2 from the updated grammar.

Tests: new `tests/BUML/metamodel/ocl/test_size_attribute.py` covers
the inherited-attribute case, the direct-attribute case, the
`if/then/else` shape from the issue body, and guards that the
existing `->size()` / `.size()` operations still parse.

subject: feat: OCL parser emits actionable error messages (closes #202)
message:
feat: OCL parser emits actionable error messages (closes #202)

The OCL checker's raw ANTLR diagnostics ("mismatched input 'then'
expecting <EOF>", "missing ')' at '<EOF>'", etc.) exposed internal
parser state and used token names that mean little to anyone writing
an OCL constraint. The specific case in issue #202 — a user who
forgot the 'if' before a 'then ... else ...' branch — surfaced as
"Error: pop from empty list", which gives no hint about what went
wrong.

`error_handling.py` now sits on top of ANTLR's error listener and
rewrites diagnostics into OCL-level hints whenever the error pattern
is recognizable:

- Missing 'if' before 'then'           -> "Did you forget the 'if'?"
- 'then' / 'else' / 'endif' outside if -> "Unexpected X without ..."
- Missing 'else' or 'endif'            -> "Expression ends before ..."
- Unbalanced parentheses               -> "Missing closing ')'"
                                           / "no matching opening '('"
- Dangling binary operator             -> "operand on the right is missing"
- Missing 'context' header             -> "must start with 'context <ClassName> ..."
- Unknown construct                    -> "Unexpected token near 'X'"

When no targeted pattern matches, the raw ANTLR message is kept as a
fallback but reformatted into the consistent "line N, column M: <msg>"
shape. Single-error exceptions drop the "Multiple OCL syntax errors:"
preamble so one-line mistakes give one-line diagnostics.

Also drops the redundant "Error: Invalid OCL syntax:" wrapper in
`ocl_checker.py` — the BOCLSyntaxError message is already a complete
sentence now.

13 new regression tests in tests/BUML/metamodel/ocl/test_error_messages.py
pinning each rewrite rule, plus positive-parse sanity checks that the
translation layer does not reject valid OCL.

subject: fix(nn): deep-review fixes — generator filename, injection, router robustness
message:
fix(nn): deep-review fixes — generator filename, injection, router robustness

Addresses a dozen findings from a multi-agent deep review of PR #453.

Critical — pytorch/tensorflow generation was 100% broken:
- generation_router._generate_nn expected 'pytorch_nn.py' / 'tf_nn.py', but
  NNCodeGenerator.generate writes '{stem}_{generation_type}.py' (e.g.
  pytorch_nn_subclassing.py). Every /generate-output for pytorch/tensorflow
  returned 400 'expected output not produced'. Compute the expected name
  from generation_type so it matches the artifact.

Critical — code-injection via user-controlled strings in generated Python:
- nn_model_builder.py interpolated layer.name / actv_func / padding_type /
  name_module_input / return_type / pooling_type / dimension / tns_type /
  dataset.name / path_data / task_type / input_format / optimizer /
  loss_function / metrics straight into single-quoted Python literals with
  no escaping. Generated files are documented as exec()-able, so a layer
  named `x'); __import__('os').system('id'); #` was a trivial RCE when a
  victim ran the download. Now every user string flows through
  _escape_python_string (from buml_code_builder.common) and metric lists
  use a new _fmt_metrics helper that quotes each item.

High — permute_in / permute_out type mismatch across the seam:
- Metamodel declares them as bool but the processor parsed via
  parse_tuple_or_int (producing ints/tuples) and the converter emitted
  them with type hint 'List'. Round-trip corrupted the values. Now: use
  parse_bool + mark_explicit in nn_diagram_processor, emit with 'bool'
  gated by _is_attr_set in nn_diagram_converter, and gate the builder on
  _is_attr_set so explicit False values round-trip too.

High — router error handling:
- validation_router.NNDiagram branch caught only ValueError; a KeyError
  on a dangling element id or TypeError from malformed attribute payload
  fell through to the generic 500 handler with no per-line detail. Widen
  to (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError) and keep splitting
  on newlines.
- conversion_router /export-buml NN branch had no try/except; any
  construction error became 500. Wrap ValueError (400) and
  (KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError) (400 'malformed') explicitly.

High — /get-json-model could not re-import NN BUML files:
- Content sniffer had branches for ClassDiagram / Agent / StateMachine /
  GUI / Project but not NN. Export an NN via /export-buml, re-upload,
  get 'Could not parse BUML file'. Add is_nn_model detection keyed on
  .add_layer / .add_tensor_op / .add_sub_nn / .add_configuration /
  .add_train_data / .add_test_data, route through nn_buml_to_json, and
  add NNDiagram to the supported-formats error message. Expose
  nn_buml_to_json and nn_model_to_json from the buml_to_json package
  __init__ so the router can import them.

Tested: full backend test suite (773 passed, NN fixtures included, 5
pre-existing skips for openpyxl-dependent tests).

   produce syntactically-valid Python — previously an NN or sub-NN with one
   of those names emitted a file that SyntaxError'd at ``exec()``.

2. Sub-NN variable collisions eliminated. ``_write_all_sub_nns`` now keys
   ``sub_nn_vars`` / ``written`` by ``id(sub_nn)`` instead of ``.name``, and
   a new ``_unique_var`` helper ensures no two top-level bindings in a file
   share a name — two siblings called ``Block`` (or ``my-net`` vs ``my_net``
   after normalization) each get their own distinct variable.

3. Project-level NN variable names. ``nn_model_to_code`` accepts a new
   ``model_var_name`` override, and ``project_to_code`` passes the suffixed
   name (``my_nn_1`` / ``my_nn_2``) down so the main NN binding matches
   what the Project(...) line references. Without this, a project with
   more than one NN raised ``NameError`` on exec.

4. ``nn_model_to_code`` seeds ``used_names`` with the main NN var and the
   reserved ``image`` / ``config`` / ``train_data`` / ``test_data`` names,
   so a sub-NN called ``config`` can't clobber the Configuration binding.
   Sub-NN names are also prefixed with the main NN's var name to avoid
   cross-NN collisions in project exports.

5. ``generation_router._generate_nn`` now catches
   ``(KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError)`` from ``process_nn_diagram``
   (matching the recent ``/export-buml`` and ``/validate-diagram`` fixes)
   so a malformed payload becomes HTTP 400 with context instead of a
   generic 500 via the exception-handler decorator.

6. ``nn_diagram_converter`` now walks transitively-reachable sub_nns
   (``_collect_all_sub_nns``) and passes ``sub_nn_ids`` into every
   ``_emit_nn_container`` call. Previously a two-level nested NN
   (A → B → C) crashed with ``KeyError`` on ``_MODULE_TYPE_MAP['NN']``
   because the inner container's ``NN``-in-``modules`` fell through to
   ``_emit_module``.

7. Dataset image symmetry. ``create_dataset`` now reconstructs ``Image``
   whenever ``shape``/``normalize`` attributes are present, not only
   when ``input_format == 'images'``. Matches the converter's emission
   rule (``if dataset.image is not None``) so a hand-authored BUML
   ``Dataset(input_format='csv', image=Image(...))`` no longer loses
   its image on buml→json→buml.

subject: fix(nn): sidecar-gated round-trip for padding/dim defaults + preserve float in layers_of_tensors
message:
fix(nn): sidecar-gated round-trip for padding/dim defaults + preserve float in layers_of_tensors

Before this change, a user who explicitly picked the metamodel default on
the following attributes saw that choice silently stripped from the
exported JSON/BUML on round-trip:

- Conv1D/2D/3D:  padding_amount (default 0), padding_type (default 'valid')
- PoolingLayer:  padding_amount, padding_type, output_dim
- FlattenLayer:  start_dim (default 1), end_dim (default -1)

The converter/builder guards looked like ``if module.padding_type and
module.padding_type != 'valid'``, which can't distinguish "user never
touched it" from "user explicitly picked the default". Fix both ends of
the pipeline:

1. Processor now calls ``mark_explicit(layer, '<attr>')`` whenever the
   attribute is present in the source JSON — for padding_amount,
   padding_type, output_dim, start_dim, end_dim.
2. Converter + builder gates now check ``_is_attr_set(module, '<attr>')
   or <legacy truthy fallback>`` so the legacy "diverges from default"
   heuristic still applies to models that bypass the editor (pure BUML
   authoring, tests), while editor-authored models always round-trip the
   user's choice.
3. Truthy ``if module.<list_attr>:`` checks replaced with
   ``is not None`` where the default can be a legitimate user-set value
   (``stride_dim``, ``kernel_dim``), matching the already-correct
   ``concatenate_dim`` pattern.

TensorOp ``layers_of_tensors`` round-trip: the metamodel declares this
as ``List[Union[str, float]]``, but the processor used to blindly strip
quotes and keep every item as a string — a value of ``[0.5, 'x']``
serialized to JSON and reparsed became ``['0.5', 'x']``. Added a
``_coerce`` helper that tries ``float()`` on each item and falls back to
the stripped string on ValueError.

subject: sec(nn): replace exec() sandbox in nn_buml_to_json with ast.parse whitelist visitor
message:
sec(nn): replace exec() sandbox in nn_buml_to_json with ast.parse whitelist visitor

The previous parser used exec() with a hand-rolled ``__builtins__``
whitelist, which is escapable via the classic attribute-traversal trick
``().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()`` — that walk returns
``subprocess.Popen`` and friends and reaches arbitrary code execution
without ever calling a builtin. The /get-json-model endpoint accepts
BUML file uploads, so this was a real server-side RCE vector.

Replace with an AST-based reconstructor:

- ``ast.parse`` the content (syntax errors surface as ValueError).
- Walk only these top-level statement shapes: ``Import`` / ``ImportFrom``
  (skipped — metamodel names come from the allowlist), simple-name
  ``Assign``, and ``Expr(Call(Attribute(Name, attr), …))`` where ``attr``
  is one of ``add_layer / add_tensor_op / add_sub_nn / add_configuration
  / add_train_data / add_test_data``.
- Evaluate only these expression shapes: Constant, Name (bound via prior
  Assign OR a metamodel class allowlist), List / Tuple / Dict / Set of
  evaluable children, UnaryOp(USub, …), and Call(Name, …) where the
  Name resolves to a metamodel class.
- Everything else (``os.system``, ``getattr``, attribute-target assignment,
  list comprehensions, lambdas, attribute chains) raises ValueError
  before any side effect.

Targets are validated BEFORE evaluating the RHS so an attribute-target
assignment (``obj.x = Class(...)``) is refused without constructing the
NN object first.

Adds test_nn_buml_to_json_safety.py with 7 tests:
- legitimate BUML parses
- ``import os; os.system(...)`` rejected
- ``().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()`` rejected
- non-allowlisted method call rejected (``main_nn.some_evil_method(…)``)
- non-allowlisted plain call rejected (``getattr(NN, '__class__')``)
- attribute-target assignment rejected
- empty input raises the descriptive "No NN instance found" error

subject: fix(nn): transitive referenced-set + literal unpack rejection + dataset empty-string guard + 6 tests
message:
fix(nn): transitive referenced-set + literal unpack rejection + dataset empty-string guard + 6 tests

Addresses four HIGH/MEDIUM findings from a fresh iter-18 review pass:

1. ``nn_buml_to_json`` built the ``referenced`` set only from direct
   ``sub_nns`` children of each top-level NN. A grandchild NN that's
   bound to a local variable (e.g. ``a.add_sub_nn(b); b.add_sub_nn(c)``
   with all three in env) slipped through the shallow check and
   triggered a spurious multi-top-level error. Walk the tree
   transitively with a stack-based DFS so every transitively-reachable
   sub-NN is counted.

2. AST visitor now explicitly rejects iterable unpacking (``*expr``)
   inside List/Tuple/Set literals and dict unpacking (``**expr``) inside
   Dict literals. Previously a Dict with ``None`` keys fell through to
   raw TypeError during evaluation (leaking as 500), and ``*`` in list
   literals hit the catch-all "Disallowed expression" instead of naming
   the unpack form.

3. ``create_dataset`` treats empty-string shape/normalize as absent,
   matching the "user cleared the field" intent. Without this, a
   Dataset with only an empty shape attribute would silently get a
   default ``Image(shape=[256,256], normalize=False)`` attached.

4. ``parse_float`` re-raises ``ValueError`` on a ``TypeError`` from
   the fallback ``float(value)`` call (e.g. when the frontend sends a
   list or dict for a numeric field). Surfaces a clear 400 instead of
   letting the mandatory-attribute check fire with a misleading
   "missing" message.

New regression tests (6, suite now 374):

- ``test_conv_permute_in_false_explicitly_marked`` — the False branch
  of the bool sidecar (pair with the existing True test).

- ``test_multi_top_level_nn_rejected`` — two unrelated NN locals raise
  with "top-level NN instances" message.
- ``test_dict_unpacking_rejected`` — ``{**{'a': 1}}`` raises
  ValueError, not TypeError.
- ``test_iterable_unpacking_in_list_rejected`` — ``[*[1,2,3]]`` raises
  ValueError.

   are not silently dropped. Matches the already-correct

fix(security/codeql): suppress py/clear-text-storage-sensitive-data on render.yaml writes

CodeQL's clear-text-storage rule flagged the two f.write(render_config)
sites in github_deploy_api.py because the render_config string contains
env-var KEY names like STREAMLIT_DB_PASSWORD, OPENAI_API_KEY, and
STREAMLIT_DB_USER. These are KEY names — Render reads them and wires
the actual secrets at deploy time. No values are written to disk.

The alert is a false positive on a heuristic scan. Suppress with the
inline lgtm comment (CodeQL still honors the legacy LGTM pragma) and
leave a comment block above each write explaining why so a future
reviewer doesn't strip the suppression and re-introduce the noise.

BAFGenerator writes the agent script as f"{model.name}.py" with case

lowercase=False). The deploy startCommand was constructing the script

matches whatever BAFGenerator wrote. The directory slug and Render

subject: fix(agent-converter): preserve intent/state name casing in personalization round-trip
message:
fix(agent-converter): preserve intent/state name casing in personalization round-trip

agent_model_builder emits lowercased Python identifiers (Muscles_intent ->
muscles_intent) bound to the original PascalCase name passed as the first
positional arg of new_intent/new_state. agent_diagram_converter only read
the keyword 'name=' arg and used the variable id for transition references,
so the round-tripped JSON for personalization variants ended up with intent
definitions in PascalCase but transition intentName references (and state
names) in lowercase. Downstream code generation then failed strict-case
intent_lookup, created an orphan Intent for the transition, and the rendered
agent script referenced an undefined variable (NameError on deploy).

Fix:
- Read positional string arg of new_state(...) for the state name.
- Track intent variable -> declared name during the AST walk and resolve
  transition intent references through it.
- Add a case-insensitive fallback in the json_to_buml intent lookup as a
  safety net (matches BUML's existing case-insensitive intent uniqueness
  validation in Agent._validate_state_intent_name_collisions).

subject: fix(nn): make NN project export importable round-trip
message:
fix(nn): make NN project export importable round-trip

Two bugs caused single-NN project exports to silently lose the diagram on
re-import:

1. nn_model_builder wrote '# Neural Network: NAME' instead of the
   '# NN MODEL #' section header that project_to_json's
   _extract_all_sections() looks for. Other builders (domain, agent, gui,
   state machine) all emit their canonical section header — NN was the
   outlier. Now writes '# NN MODEL #' like the others.

2. project_builder used _name_to_var(nm.name) to derive the Python
   variable bound in models=[...], producing names like 'neural_netwo_rk'.
   project_to_json strips trailing _\d+ and looks up the result in
   SECTION_CONFIG, which keys on 'nn_model'. The mismatch caused the
   importer's outer loop to skip the NN entirely before even checking
   for sections. Now uses _suffixed_name('nn_model', idx, n_nn) to match
   the SECTION_CONFIG key (matching how agent/gui/quantum/sm work).

subject: fix(nn): preserve diagram title across BUML round-trip
message:
fix(nn): preserve diagram title across BUML round-trip

The NN metamodel only stores a sanitized identifier-safe `name`, so the
user-facing diagram title (e.g. 'CIFAR-10 CNN') was lost the moment the
project was exported to BUML — re-import always came back as 'NN Diagram'.

Plumb the title from json_to_buml_project (which still has the raw JSON
with titles) onto the Project as `_nn_diagram_titles` (id(nn) -> title),
then have project_to_code thread that through to nn_model_to_code which
embeds it in the `# NN MODEL: "title" #` section header. The
importer's existing regex already captures the title from that header.

Also collapses the previous double-header layout (project_builder wrote
its own '# NN MODEL N: "label" #' and nn_model_builder wrote a plain
'# NN MODEL #') into a single header written exclusively by
nn_model_builder. The duplicate had been silently erasing titles in
multi-NN exports too — now both single and multi cases preserve them.

     base's source-text expression, and exposes the AST via a new ast

   - pretty_printer.py:59: same .expression -> .ast migration.

subject: fix(django generator): chdir into temp_dir before scaffolding project
message:
fix(django generator): chdir into temp_dir before scaffolding project

DjangoGenerator.generate() shells out to `django-admin startproject` with
no cwd, and several internal paths are derived from os.getcwd(). The pre-
refactor backend.py wrapped the call in chdir(temp_dir)/try-finally; the
extracted _generate_django helper in generation_router.py dropped that
guard, so the project got scaffolded in the FastAPI process's cwd while
the harvester walked an empty temp_dir/<project_name>, producing
"Django project generation failed: Output directory is empty".

Re-introduce the chdir guard, scoped to the worker thread that runs
generate(), and restore the original cwd in finally.

subject: fix(github deploy): surface GitHub API errors instead of generic 500
message:
fix(github deploy): surface GitHub API errors instead of generic 500

deploy_webapp_to_github lets httpx.HTTPStatusError fall through to the
catch-all handler, which buries the actual cause ("name already exists
on this account", expired token, rate limit) under "An internal error
occurred during GitHub deployment." and a 500. The frontend then has
nothing useful to show in the popup.

Add a dedicated httpx.HTTPStatusError branch that pulls the message out
of GitHub's response body — preferring the nested errors[*].message
that names the offending field — and re-raises with a meaningful
status: 401 / 403 pass through, 422 maps to 409 Conflict (so the UI
can offer rename/overwrite), other 4xx pass through, and 5xx becomes
502 Bad Gateway.

subject: fix(ocl): narrow OCLConstraint pretty-print exception to ImportError
message:
fix(ocl): narrow OCLConstraint pretty-print exception to ImportError

OCLConstraint.__init__ and the ast setter wrapped pretty_print() in a
broad `except Exception`, falling back to `str(expression)`. The fallback
is itself broken (OCLExpression.__str__ returns None) and the broad
catch hides real pretty-printer bugs by silently writing "None" into
Constraint.expression — a defect that would surface much later as a
mysterious "None" in downstream diagnostics.

Narrow to `except ImportError` (the only documented reason for the
deferred import), use try/else to keep the import scope local, and fall
back to repr() — at least visibly typed — only when the import itself
fails. Any other exception now propagates so a real bug surfaces at the
construction site.

subject: fix(ocl): use isinstance(OCLExpression) instead of hasattr for location copy
message:
fix(ocl): use isinstance(OCLExpression) instead of hasattr for location copy

_rewrite_pass guarded the copy_location_from() call with
hasattr(new_node, "copy_location_from"). Every rule.rewrite() returns
an OCLExpression (verified across rules/_helpers.py and each rule
module), so the hasattr is duck-typing where the real contract is
"new_node is an OCLExpression."

Replace with isinstance(new_node, OCLExpression). This asserts the
actual contract, matches the same check used in clone.py:30, and
crashes loudly if a future rule ever returns something unexpected
(e.g. None) instead of silently skipping the location copy.

subject: fix(ocl): drop bare except around ctx.getText() in BOCLVisitorImpl.visit
message:
fix(ocl): drop bare except around ctx.getText() in BOCLVisitorImpl.visit

The visitor's source-location population wrapped ctx.getText() in
`try: ... except Exception: pass`. ANTLR's ParserRuleContext.getText()
concatenates token text from the subtree and does not raise under
normal parses; the bare except was defensive against a problem that
doesn't exist and would silently hide any real failure.

Drop the try/except. If getText() ever raises, the error surfaces at
the parse site rather than being swallowed into a None source_text.

feat(wme-ocl): wire Method.pre/post + AST-backed invariants through the converter

Make the WME class diagram converter route OCL constraints by their JSON
``kind`` field — invariants land on ``domain_model.constraints``;
preconditions and postconditions land on ``Method.pre`` / ``Method.post``
via ``targetMethodId``. Builds on the metamodel work landed on
development (PR #528): ``Method.pre`` / ``Method.post`` first-class fields,
AST-backed ``OCLConstraint``, and ``parse_ocl(...)``.

Backend changes:

* ``parsers/ocl_parser.py``
  - new ``parse_ocl_body(body, kind, name, class_, model, method=None)``
    helper that synthesizes the BOCL grammar's required header
    (``context C inv name:`` for invariants, ``context C::m(p:T) pre|post:``
    for pre/post — different shapes mandated by the BOCL grammar) before
    calling ``parse_ocl``.
  - rewritten ``process_ocl_constraints`` returns AST-backed
    ``OCLConstraint`` (was bare ``Constraint``) and skips malformed
    blocks with a warning instead of producing junk text. Kept on the
    legacy path for projects whose textareas still contain the full
    ``context X inv name: expr`` form.

* ``json_to_buml/class_diagram_processor.py``
  - ``_process_classes`` now returns ``(class_id_to_class,
    method_id_to_method)`` element-id maps; the maps are stashed on
    ``domain_model._class_element_ids`` and ``_method_element_ids`` so
    ``buml_to_json`` can re-emit the original UUIDs (without this,
    every BUML→JSON cycle silently broke ``targetMethodId`` references).
  - rewritten ``_process_constraints`` routes by ``kind``: invariants are
    parsed via ``parse_ocl_body`` and added to ``domain_model.constraints``;
    pre/post resolve their target method via ``targetMethodId`` and call
    ``method.add_pre`` / ``add_post``. Auto-generates names when
    ``constraintName`` is absent. Skip-with-warning on parse failure,
    missing link, or orphan target method.
  - the existing legacy textarea path (no ``kind`` field) continues to work.

* ``buml_to_json/class_diagram_converter.py``
  - reuses stashed element ids when emitting classes and methods.
  - existing invariant emitter tags ``kind: "invariant"`` plus
    ``constraintName`` so the next ingest takes the kind-aware path.
  - new emission pass walks every class's methods' ``pre`` / ``post`` and
    emits one ``ClassOCLConstraint`` element + ``ClassOCLLink`` per

* ``validators/ocl_checker.py``

subject: refactor(wme-ocl): pivot OCL ingest/emit to canonical full-text constraints
message:
refactor(wme-ocl): pivot OCL ingest/emit to canonical full-text constraints

Replace the body-only intermediate shape introduced one commit ago.
The textbox on the canvas now holds the complete OCL block — header
plus body — exactly as it appears in the BOCL grammar:

  context Book inv book_pages_positive: self.pages > 0
  context Book::decrease_stock(qty: int) pre: qty > 0
  context Book::decrease_stock(qty: int) post: self.stock >= 0

Driver: Jordi's downstream metamodel consumer reads the full OCL source
text to extract the constraint name and detect duplicates. The body-only
shape hid the name inside metadata that his parser doesn't see, so the
canonical wire format goes back to full text.

Backend changes:

* ``parsers/ocl_parser.py``
  - Drop ``parse_ocl_body``; replace with ``parse_constraint_text(text,
    model)`` that inspects the BOCL header to extract kind / class /
    optional method / optional name, resolves the class manually, and
    delegates lex/parse to ``parse_ocl(...)`` with an explicit
    ``context_class`` (the upstream auto-detect regex doesn't handle
    the ``Class::method(params)`` segment in pre/post headers, so we
    bypass it).
  - ``process_ocl_constraints`` now returns a list of
    ``(kind, OCLConstraint, class_name, method_name)`` routing tuples,
    one per ``context X ...`` block in the textarea blob. Malformed
    blocks still skip-with-warning.
  - Add ``legacy_body_only_to_text(...)`` — a one-direction shim used
    only on ingest, to lift JSON files saved during the previous
    iteration (body-only ``constraint`` plus ``kind`` /
    ``targetMethodId`` / ``constraintName`` siblings) to canonical
    full text before parsing. Self-deprecates per file: any project
    saved through the new emission path drops the legacy fields and
    never hits this shim again.

* ``json_to_buml/class_diagram_processor.py``
  - Replace the kind/targetMethodId/ClassOCLLink-walk routing in
    ``_process_constraints`` with a single loop that:
      1. coerces each box's textarea to canonical full text via
         ``_ocl_box_to_full_text`` (fast-path when already canonical;
         legacy shim otherwise),
      2. calls ``process_ocl_constraints`` to parse + classify,
      3. routes invariants into ``domain_model.constraints`` and
         pre/post into ``Method.pre`` / ``Method.post`` via a
         ``(class_name, method_name) -> Method`` index built from the
         metamodel (Class.methods names are unique per class).
  - Drop the ``_class_element_ids`` / ``_method_element_ids`` stashes
    that existed solely to keep ``targetMethodId`` references stable
    across save/load. With full-text, references are name-based and
    stability is automatic.

* ``buml_to_json/class_diagram_converter.py``
  - Drop ``saved_class_ids`` / ``saved_method_ids`` element-id reuse;
    fresh UUIDs are fine again.
  - Replace the kind/targetMethodId/constraintName fields on emitted
    ``ClassOCLConstraint`` boxes with a single ``constraint`` field
    holding the rebuilt full text.
  - Add ``_emit_full_ocl_text(constraint, kind, method=None)`` to
    reconstruct the BOCL header from the constraint's context class,
    name, and (for pre/post) the owning method's signature.
  - Pre/post emission walks every class's methods' ``.pre`` and
    ``.post`` lists exactly as before — the text shape is what
    changed, not the structural layout of emitted elements.

* ``parsers/__init__.py`` — re-exports updated.

Tests (test_ocl_pre_post.py): rewritten end-to-end. Drops the now-gone
``parse_ocl_body_*`` and method-element-id-stability tests; adds tests
for ``parse_constraint_text`` header extraction, multi-block parsing,
unknown-method skip-with-warning, body-only legacy ingest via the shim,
metadata stripping on emit, and full-text round-trip stability.

subject: refactor(ocl): single canonical text on Constraint.expression
message:
refactor(ocl): single canonical text on Constraint.expression

Consolidates the OCL constraint pipeline around a single contract:
``constraint.expression`` carries the full canonical OCL text
(``context X (inv|pre|post) [name]: body``) from the moment a
constraint is parsed, through every storage, transport, validation,
and evaluation step. No more body-only-vs-full-text divergence.

Eliminates three reconstruction layers and one mutation hack that
all existed to paper over OCLConstraint storing pretty-printed
body-only on its expression field:

- ocl_parser.parse_constraint_text: one-line override
  ``constraint.expression = text`` after parse_ocl().
- ocl_checker: drops _method_signature / _already_full_text /
  _canonical_invariant_text / _canonical_method_contract_text and
  the swap-and-restore around parser.evaluate(). Just uses
  constraint.expression directly. Adds _ensure_canonical_expression
  as a narrow legacy fallback for old BUML files (deprecated:
  removal target 2026-Q4).
- buml_to_json: drops _emit_full_ocl_text. Emits
  constraint.expression verbatim for both class invariants and
  method contracts.

While here:

- domain_model_builder now walks each method's pre/post lists and
  emits ``Method.add_pre(...)`` / ``add_post(...)`` calls. Without
  this loop, BUML export silently dropped every method contract
  on round-trip — confirmed against
  library__full_stack__project (1).py.
- json_to_buml.class_diagram_processor warns on duplicate
  (Class, method_name) pairs so silent overload collisions in
  pre/post routing are surfaced.
- legacy_body_only_to_text gets a deprecation note pointing at
  2026-Q4 removal.
- Validator skips evaluation of pre/post against an object model
  (the BOCL evaluator can't bind method parameters without a
  runtime invocation — would raise NameError silently). Pre/post
  remain syntax-checked.

Tests: 1061 backend tests pass (test_ocl_pre_post.py adjusted to
the new ``expression`` contract). Validated against:
- Library_OCL.json (7 inv + 3 pre + 1 post): 11/11 ✅
- team_player_ocl.json (2 inv): 2/2 ✅
- Library_Complete.json (1 inv): 1/1 ✅
- Legacy body-only BUML: 7/7 ✅ (via fallback)
- Library_OCL → BUML → re-import → validate: 11/11 ✅, pre/post
  routing preserved (Book.decrease_stock.pre = 2, .post = 1).

subject: fix(ocl): de-dup constraint names across OCL boxes instead of crashing
message:
fix(ocl): de-dup constraint names across OCL boxes instead of crashing

Two ``ClassOCLConstraint`` boxes that parse to the same constraint
name (whether typed by the user or auto-generated by
``process_ocl_constraints``) used to crash ``_process_constraints``:
``DomainModel.constraints`` rejects duplicate names with a
``ValueError``, and the assignment ``domain_model.constraints =
set(...) | extra_invariants`` had no guard around it, so the error
escaped the whole conversion.

De-dup by name before assigning, keep the first occurrence, and
emit a ``Warning: duplicate constraint name 'X' across OCL boxes;
keeping the first occurrence`` so users can spot the collision in
the validator output.

Discovered by a 2000-constraint stress test (5 parallel agents
exercising invariants, pre/post, multi-block, evaluator, and
adversarial inputs); this was the only case that produced an
uncaught exception across ~2023 inputs.

Tests: new ``test_duplicate_constraint_name_across_boxes_does_not_crash``
in ``test_ocl_pre_post.py``. Full suite remains green (1062 passed).

subject: fix(ocl): preserve insertion order when de-duping constraint names
message:
fix(ocl): preserve insertion order when de-duping constraint names

The de-dup loop iterated over a set, whose iteration order is not
guaranteed across Python versions. Locally Python 3.11 happened to
yield insertion order so 'first wins' worked; CI Python 3.11 gave a
different order and the second occurrence won, breaking
test_duplicate_constraint_name_across_boxes_does_not_crash.

Switch extra_invariants from set to list so iteration order
matches the source elements.items() order (insertion order on
modern Python dicts), making 'first wins' deterministic across
environments.

subject: fix(ocl): blockers from PR #529 deep review
message:
fix(ocl): blockers from PR #529 deep review

Three independent issues called out by the multi-agent review.

1. Identifier injection via constraint/method names in BUML codegen.
   ``constraint.name`` and ``method.name`` flowed straight into
   Python identifier positions on the LHS of assignments — a name
   like ``x=1;import os;os.system('id')#`` (no spaces, no hyphens,
   passes ``NamedElement.name``'s setter) would land verbatim in
   code that gets ``exec()``'d. Route every identifier through
   ``safe_var_name`` (existing helper in ``common.py``); add a
   ``_method_var_name(method)`` shim and apply it at all five
   emit sites (was 5 different copies of ``method.name.split('(')[0]``).

2. Pre/post boxes lost their ``description`` on JSON↔BUML round-trip.
   ``buml_to_json/class_diagram_converter.py`` emitted ``description``
   only on the invariant path; method-contract boxes silently dropped
   the field. Mirror the invariant emit. Also drops the hard-coded
   ``"name": "OCL"`` field that was unique to the pre/post path
   (invariants don't set it; reviewer flagged the asymmetry).

3. Inline ``--`` comments lost on round-trip. ``_extract_inline_description``
   used to strip ``--`` from the canonical text; the BUML→JSON
   emitter never re-injected it, so a user's
   ``context X inv: self.x > 0 -- must be positive`` collapsed to
   ``context X inv: self.x > 0`` after the first emit. Now the
   helper returns ``(stripped, description)`` — the parser still
   sees a stripped form (``parse_ocl``'s visitor rejects trailing
   comment tokens, even though the lexer skips them) — but
   ``process_ocl_constraints`` overrides ``constraint.expression``
   with the comment-preserving canonical line so emit is bit-stable.

Tests: 1062/1062 pass. ``test_inline_comment_takes_precedence_over_default``
now asserts ``"-- Inline wins" in constraint.expression`` (the new
contract), where it previously asserted the comment was stripped.

subject: fix(ocl): address review findings on pre/post wire-up
message:
fix(ocl): address review findings on pre/post wire-up

* Embed auto-generated invariant names back into expression so the
  next BUML→JSON→BUML cycle parses out the same name instead of
  generating a fresh ``counter_blockidx`` suffix.
* Tighten the OCL header regex consumer to ignore the optional name
  segment for pre/post — only invariants carry a name in BOCL.
* Walk the inheritance chain when building the
  ``(class, method) → Method`` index so a precondition written as
  ``context Sub::base_method() pre: ...`` resolves to a method
  declared on a parent class instead of warn-skipping.
* Narrow the residual ``except Exception`` in OCL element processing
  to ``(BOCLSyntaxError, ValueError)`` so programmer errors propagate
  instead of being swallowed.
* Sort method_contracts in domain_model_builder so the emitted Python
  is byte-stable (matches how invariants and other emissions sort).
* Drop defensive ``getattr`` / ``hasattr`` guards on metamodel
  attributes that the metamodel now guarantees (``Class.methods``,
  ``Method.pre``, ``Method.post``).
* Walk method pre/post in DomainModel._validate_constraints so a
  precondition with a stale or external context is flagged the same
  way an invariant would be.
* Tighten the round-trip stress test to also assert link wiring and
  description survive each cycle, not just constraint text.

currentColor fallback on the OCL kind badge.

subject: docs(ocl): clarify pre/post BOCL headers and editor authoring flow
message:
docs(ocl): clarify pre/post BOCL headers and editor authoring flow

Pre/post examples in ocl.rst, parsing.rst, and examples/ocl.rst all used
``context Account inv: ...`` headers and overrode .name afterwards. That
parses (the inner expression is what add_pre/add_post stores) but it's
pedagogically wrong — readers copy the inv: header and then trip on the
WME's parse_constraint_text, which routes by the kind keyword in the
header. Switch every pre/post example to the canonical
``context Class::method(p: Type) pre|post:`` form.

Also:

- Replace the single misleading invariant example
  (``context library inv inv1: self.books>0``) with a header-shape
  reference table covering all four BOCL kinds (inv, pre, post, init)
  and one canonical example for each.
- Add an "Authoring constraints in the Web Modeling Editor" section to
  ocl.rst — the page used to be entirely Python-API-flavoured even
  though most users edit OCL through the editor's constraint box. New
  section names the «inv»/«pre»/«post» badge and the description field.
- parsing.rst: note that the auto-detect regex only handles the
  invariant header shape; pre/post/init must pass context_class
  explicitly. Same callout in ocl.rst beside the pre/post Python
  example.
- normalization.rst: tighten the termination claim — each rule
  strictly decreases the lexicographic measure, max_iterations exists
  to surface a developer bug (a rule that violates the measure)
  rather than to bound a "guaranteed" termination.

subject: feat(agents): support multi-LLM agents with a designated default
message:
feat(agents): support multi-LLM agents with a designated default

  Adds multi-LLM support to the BAF agent generator. An agent can declare
  zero or more LLMs and mark one as the default; consumers that don't
  specify a per-action LLM (LLMReply, DBReply, RAG, intent classifier,
  ReasoningState) resolve to it at code-generation time.

  Metamodel (BUML/metamodel/state_machine/agent.py):
  - Adds Agent.llms, Agent.default_llm_name, new_llm, set_default_llm.
  - First registered LLM is the auto-default; set_default_llm overrides.
  - _check accepts empty llm_name as "use default" and only flags unknown
    names. ReasoningState.llm is no longer strictly required at validation
    (empty signals "use default at codegen time").

  Generator template (generators/agents/templates/baf_agent_template.py.j2):
  - Renames the internal default variable reply_llm -> default_llm; emits
    one Python variable per agent.llms entry with default_llm aliased to
    the registered default.
  - LLM-based intent classifier resolves its LLM dynamically (config pick
    -> agent default -> first registered -> '') instead of hardcoding
    gpt-5-nano.
  - RAG falls back to agent.default_llm_name instead of gpt-4o-mini.
  - No-LLM case: emits `default_llm = None` and uses '' for string-typed
    llm_name fields. Drops the legacy config['llm'].provider/model
    synthesis that fabricated an LLMOpenAI from the frontend default
    config on blank projects.

  Converters (utilities/web_modeling_editor/backend/services/converters/):
  - json_to_buml extracts AgentLLM elements and applies
    config.default_llm_name from the diagram config block.
  - buml_to_json round-trips agent.llms back to the editor.

  BUML code builder (utilities/buml_code_builder/agent_model_builder.py):
  - Emits new_llm(...) per LLM and set_default_llm only when the chosen
    default differs from the auto-default.
  - Drops the `llm = LLMOpenAI(name='gpt-4o-mini', ...)` synthesis when no
    LLMs are registered (it self-registered on the agent during exec and
    poisoned agent.llms before BAFGenerator ran); now emits
    `default_llm = None`.

message:
fix(supabase): sanitize identifiers/strings, validate user_root, add tests

Closes the three blockers surfaced by review:

1. SQL identifier injection
   Every name flowing into the SQL template now passes through a generator-
   side _safe_ident() that doubles embedded double-quotes and rejects NUL/
   CR/LF. Applied uniformly to class names, attribute names, association
   end names, FK column names, junction-table names, and enum type names
   so the template renders pre-sanitized values verbatim.

2. Enum literal injection
   _safe_string() doubles single quotes in enum literal values before they
   reach the 'CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM' template. NUL/CR/LF rejected.

3. user_root not validated at the HTTP boundary
   /generate-output now rejects user_root values that do not match
   ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,62}$ with HTTP 400, so a malformed config
   surfaces a clean error instead of flowing through the generator.

Adds tests/generators/supabase/ with 8 cases covering: structural emission
on the shared library_book_author_model fixture, the M:N junction path,
the auth.users mirror trigger, denormalized user_id + RLS policies,
UUID PK + gen_random_uuid(), the two injection blockers, NUL/newline
rejection, and the migration-style filename format.

All 8 new tests pass; full generator suite (190 tests) green; ruff clean.

subject: feat(bpmn): add BPMN metamodel to B-UML
message:
feat(bpmn): add BPMN metamodel to B-UML

Adds a BPMN metamodel as a first-class B-UML diagram type alongside
Class / State / Agent. Covers the WME BPMN editor's element set with a
spec-shaped class hierarchy.

Metamodel (besser/BUML/metamodel/bpmn/, single file ~26 classes, 5 enums):
- BPMNElement.name relaxed (BPMN allows empty/duplicate names; identity
  is by object).
- Orthogonal event model: direction (CATCH/THROW) x event_definition,
  enforced construction-time via a legality table; StartEvent/EndEvent
  pin direction.
- Four flow classes under BPMNConnectingObject: SequenceFlow,
  MessageFlow, Association, DataAssociation.
- SequenceFlow.is_default + Activity/Gateway.default_flow with the
  spec's source-restriction rule; default_flow is derived from the
  outgoing flows so the two views can't desync.
- Diagram-Interchange info stays out of the abstract syntax;
  BPMNElement carries an opaque `layout` passthrough so converters can
  round-trip WME bounds/path/id without polluting the metamodel.
- BPMNModel.validate() collects errors/warnings (E1-E11, W1-W4)
  matching the house pattern.
- Transaction subclasses SubProcess (per BPMN spec); SubProcess uses
  flow_nodes/sequence_flows for duck-type compatibility with Process.

Tests (tests/BUML/metamodel/bpmn/, 45 tests, all passing):
- conftest fixtures: pool-less Start->Task->End, two-pool collaboration
  with a message flow, exclusive gateway with a default flow.
- Coverage across construction validation, derived default_flow
  invariants, validate() rules, identity, and Project integration.
- Ruff clean on the CI rule set.

subject: feat(bpmn): add BPMN converters between WME JSON and B-UML
message:
feat(bpmn): add BPMN converters between WME JSON and B-UML

Wires BPMN diagrams into the WME backend conversion pipeline alongside
the other diagram types. Mirrors the JSON ↔ BUML converter pair used by
class / state-machine / agent diagrams; uses the diagram-type string
BPMNDiagram (consistent with ClassDiagram, StateMachineDiagram, …).

JSON → BUML (services/converters/json_to_buml/bpmn_diagram_processor.py):
- 3-pass: build nodes, reconstruct containment from the WME owner chain
  (lane → pool process; pool → its process; sub-process → itself; null →
  synthetic Process), build flows.
- ConversionError on structural failures (missing model key, unknown
  WME element / enum / flowType). Non-fatal cases (dangling endpoint,
  illegal isDefault) log and skip / downgrade — match the house pattern.
- WME ids and bounds ride in BPMNElement.layout (decision D8) so the
  metamodel stays id-free; converter never needs a separate id-mapping
  side table.

BUML → JSON (services/converters/buml_to_json/bpmn_diagram_converter.py):
- id_for() reuses the WME id stashed in layout, mints a uuid otherwise —
  round-trip stable per element.
- Deterministic walk via besser.utilities.sort_by_timestamp (BPMN names
  are not unique — sorting by name isn't an option).
- Layout fallback: when a freshly-built model has no bounds, a per-class
  grid lays nodes out and layout_calculator computes flow paths.

Shared event mapping (services/converters/bpmn_event_mapping.py):
- WME flat eventType ↔ orthogonal (EventDirection × EventDefinitionType)
  — single source of truth for both directions, covering every row of
  Appendix A in .claude/bpmn/03-bpmn-converters-guide.md.

Constants (constants/constants.py):
- BPMN_DIAGRAM_TYPE, BPMN_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE, BPMN_ELEMENT_TYPES,
  BPMN_FLOW_TYPES — shared between the processor and converter.

Router (routers/conversion_router.py):
- /export-buml gains a BPMNDiagram branch that parses + validates the
  payload. The .py emit step requires the BPMN code-builder (next guide,
  04-) and surfaces a clear ConversionError until that lands, so the
  endpoint shape is final and callers get a specific message rather
  than a 500.

Project converters:
- json_to_buml/project_converter.py: full BPMN registration — projects
  with BPMN diagrams round-trip end to end on the JSON → BUML side.
- buml_to_json/project_converter.py: only the harmless additions
  (default titles + diagram_defaults) so projects with empty BPMN
  diagrams export cleanly. SECTION_CONFIG / SINGLE_DIAGRAM_KEYWORDS
  routing through bpmn_to_json(content) is gated on 04-.

Subpackage exports updated in services/converters/__init__.py and the
two side __init__.py s. The bpmn_diagram_processor import is placed
before project_converter inside json_to_buml/__init__.py to avoid a
circular import (project_converter does `from . import process_bpmn_diagram`).

Tests (tests/utilities/web_modeling_editor/backend/services/converters/):
- test_bpmn_converters.py: 82 tests — JSON → BUML construction, BUML →
  JSON envelope shape, round-trip identity on four hand-written fixtures
  (pool-less, two-pool collaboration, gateway-with-default, sub-process),
  every Appendix A event row in both directions, and error handling.
- conftest.py mocks optional backend deps (bocl, fastapi-related, …)
  only when they aren't installed locally — pattern copied from
  tests/utilities/web_modeling_editor/converters/nn/conftest.py so test
  collection works in minimal environments.

All 127 BPMN tests pass (45 metamodel + 82 converter); ruff clean on the
CI rule set across all touched files.

subject: feat(bpmn): add BPMN code builder + close out converter wiring
message:
feat(bpmn): add BPMN code builder + close out converter wiring

Adds the BPMNModel -> executable Python builder and the bpmn_to_json
file-import wrapper, then finishes the wiring 03- left gated. Closes
the BPMN backend track (metamodel + converters + builder + endpoints).

Builder (besser/utilities/buml_code_builder/bpmn_model_builder.py):
- bpmn_model_to_code(model, file_path=None, model_var_name="bpmn_model")
  emits a self-contained .py module that exec-recovers an identical
  BPMNModel.
- Option-b emission (per 04- guide and state_machine_builder
  convention): build empty containers first, then add_* calls. Strict
  ordering so every add_* call has its arguments already in scope;
  recursive _emit_container handles SubProcess nesting.
- _NameDispenser per metamodel object - BPMN names can be empty,
  whitespace, or duplicated (decision D5), so variable identifiers are
  derived from class + sanitised-name + collision suffix.
- Layout passthrough as a per-object one-liner when present - keeps
  the .py round-trip lossless. Skipped when None so freshly-built
  models emit clean code.
- Imports computed dynamically: only the metamodel symbols actually
  used end up in the import block. Determinism via sort_by_timestamp.

Wrapper (services/converters/buml_to_json/bpmn_diagram_converter.py):
- bpmn_to_json(content) execs the source in a fresh namespace and
  delegates to the existing bpmn_object_to_json. Catches SyntaxError /
  NameError / TypeError / ValueError and re-wraps as ConversionError
  so handle_endpoint_errors maps them to a 400. RuntimeError from
  arbitrary user code is intentionally NOT caught (per 04- guide - we
  do not want to mask genuinely unexpected failures with a 400).
- _find_bpmn_model prefers the conventional bpmn_model var; falls
  back to any BPMNModel instance in the namespace.

Router (routers/conversion_router.py):
- /export-buml BPMN branch now writes a real .py via
  bpmn_model_to_code (the 03- ConversionError placeholder is gone).
- /get-json-model gains BPMN keyword detection (bpmnmodel(,
  .add_process(, .add_flow_node(, .add_sequence_flow() + an elif
  branch that calls bpmn_to_json. The is_project parsing block also
  recognises BPMNDiagram so a Project upload containing a BPMN
  diagram returns it.
- Unsupported-format error string updated to mention BPMNDiagram.

Project converters:
- buml_to_json/project_converter.py: SECTION_CONFIG bpmn_model entry,
  ALL_SECTION_KEYWORDS adds BPMN, _convert_section dispatches to
  bpmn_to_json, SINGLE_DIAGRAM_KEYWORDS recognises BPMN single-diagram
  files, _build_project_from_single_diagram dispatches to bpmn_to_json,
  and the unsupported-single-diagram error string mentions BPMNDiagram.
- buml_code_builder/project_builder.py: BPMNModel instances are
  collected into a bpmn_models bucket and emitted via
  bpmn_model_to_code. Variable prefix bpmn_model matches the
  importer's SECTION_CONFIG so round-trips pair cleanly. Mirrors
  state_machine's no-project-level-header-for-single pattern (the
  builder's own banner is the section marker).

Subpackage exports updated in buml_code_builder/__init__.py,
services/converters/buml_to_json/__init__.py, and
services/converters/__init__.py.

Tests:
- tests/utilities/buml_code_builder/test_bpmn_model_builder.py - 18
  tests covering builder validity (compiles), exec round-trip on all
  four 03- fixtures, name-collision resolution, layout passthrough,
  banner / import-block stability, determinism (same model -> same
  source; walk order follows timestamp).
- tests/utilities/web_modeling_editor/backend/services/converters/
  test_bpmn_converters.py - 5 new tests for the bpmn_to_json wrapper:
  full round-trip via the builder for all four fixtures, exec
  failure -> ConversionError, missing-BPMNModel -> ConversionError,
  finds the model under any var name, syntax error -> ConversionError.

156 BPMN tests pass (45 metamodel + 82 converter + 29 builder/wrapper);
509 tests pass across the full converter / builder / metamodel sweep.
Ruff clean on the CI rule set across all touched files. Run via
`conda run -n besser python -m pytest ...` per memory
[[backend-tests-use-besser-env]].

message:
feat(metamodel): add UML Component metamodel + tests

Adds besser/BUML/metamodel/uml_component/ as a first-class B-UML diagram
type, implementing the design locked in
.claude/component-deployment/01-component-deployment-design.md (D1..D14).

Metamodel (uml_component.py, ~880 lines):

* Base hierarchy: ComponentElement(NamedElement) with relaxed name setter
  (free-text labels — spaces / colons / empty allowed) and opaque `layout`
  passthrough; ComponentModel(Model) with relaxed name; ComponentRelationship
  abstract base with overridable endpoint type-check seam.
* Components: Component (with agent_category / locality / is_human /
  realizes / process_model_refs / parent), Subsystem (Component +
  children container, maintains parent back-reference), Skill, Tool.
* Standalone elements: Interface, Permission (with non-empty scope).
* Relationships: InterfaceProvided / InterfaceRequired (Component → Interface),
  ComponentDependency (Component → Component), AgenticEdge (typed dependency
  with kind enum + permissions list, per-kind construction-time endpoint
  type rules — Q11=c).
* Enums: AgentCategory (NONE/SOLUTION/SUPERVISION/CONSENSUS/COLLABORATION —
  generic role names, not framework-specific), Locality (LOCAL/EXTERNAL/HYBRID
  per NR-5), AgenticEdgeKind (8 kinds covering directive D1's edge set +
  agent→capability wiring + Tool→Skill realization).
* ComponentModel.validate() — collect-don't-throw, returns
  {success, errors, warnings}. Errors E1..E13, warnings W1..W7 per
  01- §4.1. Dangling cross-diagram refs (W4/W5) are project-level
  promotion targets, left for 04-.

Tests (49 tests, all passing — 0.08s):

* Group 1: construction validation (relaxed names, type-checked enums,
  list[str] coercion, dict|None layout).
* Group 2: Subsystem containment + parent back-reference + all_components()
  traversal.
* Group 3: relationship endpoint construction-time TypeErrors.
* Group 4: per-kind AgenticEdge endpoint rules + kind setter re-validation.
* Group 5: validate() E1..E13 — dangling refs, agent-only-as-agent-endpoint,
  duplicate names, empty Permission scope, orphan parent Subsystem.
* Group 6: warnings W1..W7.
* Group 7: object-identity contract.
* Plus accessor / repr / type-check coverage.

Ruff clean on the CI ruleset
(F841/F401/F541/F811/E711/E721/E731/E741 — see .github/workflows/ci.yml).

Cross-references stay decoupled per D13: realizes / process_model_refs are
List[str] of stable IDs; resolution happens in the project-level converter
(04-, future track). Component metamodel is independent of any other (no
BPMN / structural-Class imports), so this commit lands cleanly on a branch
without the BPMN baseline.

subject: feat(metamodel): add UML Deployment metamodel + tests
message:
feat(metamodel): add UML Deployment metamodel + tests

Adds besser/BUML/metamodel/uml_deployment/ as a first-class B-UML diagram
type, implementing the design locked in
.claude/component-deployment/01-component-deployment-design.md (D1..D14).

Distinct from the existing besser/BUML/metamodel/deployment/ package
(cloud-infra, K8s Cluster / K8s Deployment / Node-with-IPs / Terraform-
facing) which stays untouched and load-bearing. The new uml_deployment
package models UML 2.5 Deployment notation (Node / Artifact /
DeploymentRelation / CommunicationPath) with an agentic stereotype
profile aligned with uml_component.

Naming-clash mitigations (00- §8):

* UML 2.5 'Node' and 'DeploymentModel' share bare class names with the
  cloud-infra package. Python namespacing resolves via the qualified
  import path; documented in the module docstring.
* UML 2.5 calls the artifact-on-node relationship 'Deployment'. The
  cloud-infra package already has a Deployment class (K8s), so this
  metamodel uses 'DeploymentRelation' to disambiguate.

Metamodel (uml_deployment.py, ~830 lines):

* Base hierarchy: DeploymentElement(NamedElement) with relaxed name
  setter and opaque `layout` passthrough; DeploymentModel(Model);
  DeploymentRelationship abstract base with endpoint type-check seam.
* Elements: Node (with NodeKind enum: GENERIC/DEVICE/EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT,
  nested_artifacts + nested_nodes containers, parent back-ref),
  Artifact (with locality, manifests cross-diagram Component IDs, parent
  back-ref), Interface.
* Relationships: DeploymentRelation (Artifact → Node, carries reused
  structural.Multiplicity per D6), CommunicationPath (Node ↔ Node),
  DeploymentDependency (plain UML), InterfaceProvided / InterfaceRequired
  (Node|Artifact → Interface).
* Enums: NodeKind, Locality (mirrors uml_component's Locality for
  semantic symmetry; kept as a separate class per the
  metamodels-are-independently-usable principle).
* DeploymentModel.validate() — collect-don't-throw, returns
  {success, errors, warnings}. Errors E1..E8, warnings W1..W4 per
  01- §4.2.

Reuses structural.Multiplicity (decision D6 / Q5=a+c) so '[3]' /
'[1..*]' artifact counts (R-06, R-20) work via the proven
structural-metamodel primitive. UNLIMITED_MAX_MULTIPLICITY supports
the upper-unbounded case.

Tests (41 tests, all passing — 0.07s):

* Group 1: construction validation.
* Group 2: Node nested_artifacts / nested_nodes containment + parent
  back-reference (incl. anti-self-containment).
* Group 3: per-class endpoint construction-time TypeErrors.
* Group 4: Multiplicity reuse — default [1..1], Code Tester [3]
  (R-20 load-bearing test), [1..*] via UNLIMITED, type-checking.
* Group 5: validate() E1..E8 — dangling refs, orphan parents,
  duplicate node names, multiplicity-bounds safety net.
* Group 6: warnings W1..W4 + UNP fixture cleanliness.
* Group 7: object-identity contract.
* Plus accessor / repr / type-check coverage.

The unp_topology_model fixture in conftest.py round-trips the
worked-example UNP scenario §6 (developer workstation, UNP sandbox,
CI runner [3], external LLM host) — the load-bearing pressure test
that thesis directive D2 (count belongs on Deployment) settles
cleanly.

Ruff clean on the CI ruleset
(F841/F401/F541/F811/E711/E721/E731/E741).

Cross-references stay decoupled per D13: Artifact.manifests is
List[str] of stable Component IDs; project-level resolution happens
in the converter (04-, future track). This metamodel does not import
uml_component or any other diagram metamodel; only structural for
Multiplicity reuse.

subject: feat(bpmn): add SEAA'25 agentic extension (AgenticTask / Gateway / Lane)
message:
feat(bpmn): add SEAA'25 agentic extension (AgenticTask / Gateway / Lane)

Adds the SEAA'25 BPMN agentic extension as a sibling module to the
vanilla BPMN base. Implements the three stereotype-as-subclass
primitives from Ait et al., SEAA'25 — AgenticTask, AgenticGateway,
AgenticLane — following the locked design in
.claude/bpmn-agentic/01-... v3 and the implementation plan in
.claude/bpmn-agentic/02-....

Metamodel (besser/BUML/metamodel/bpmn/agentic.py, 541 LOC):
- 5 enums, values mirror Adem's WME fork (branch dev/bpmn,
  common/types.ts) verbatim so the future JSON converter is a
  string-passthrough: ReflectionMode (none/self/cross/human),
  CollaborationMode (voting/role/debate/competition), MergingStrategy
  (7 values per paper Table 2: majority / absolute-majority /
  minority / leader-driven / composed / fastest / most-complete),
  GatewayRole (diverging/merging), AgentRole (worker/manager).
- AgenticTask(Task): reflection_mode + trust_score (paper §4.2,
  Fig 3b).
- AgenticGateway(Gateway): gateway_type constrained to PARALLEL or
  INCLUSIVE only (paper §4.3 excludes EXCLUSIVE / COMPLEX /
  EVENT_BASED) via a setter override on the inherited attribute.
  Carries gateway_role + collaboration_mode + merging_strategy +
  trust_score with two tri-attribute invariants auto-maintained by
  the setters: (INV-A) merging_strategy is None iff gateway_role ==
  DIVERGING; (INV-B) when set, must be in
  _LEGAL_MERGING_STRATEGIES[collaboration_mode] (paper §4.3
  Table 2, including the rule that debate borrows from voting + role
  strategies).
- AgenticLane(Lane): role + trust_score (paper §4.1, Fig 3a).
- Trust score: int [0, 100], ValueError on out-of-range (BUML house
  style, no silent clamping; the future converter will clamp on
  import to bridge WME's tolerant data).
- Base bpmn.py is byte-identical to feature/bpmn. The only
  modification outside agentic.py is one additive line in
  __init__.py.

Tests (tests/BUML/metamodel/bpmn/test_agentic.py, 74 cases after
parametrize fanout, all green):
- Enum integrity for all five enums.
- AgenticTask: defaults, isinstance(Task), all four reflection
  values, trust_score range + type checks, inherited Task kwargs.
- AgenticGateway: defaults, isinstance(Gateway), gateway_type
  eligibility (accepts PARALLEL/INCLUSIVE, rejects EXCLUSIVE /
  COMPLEX / EVENT_BASED), eligibility check fires post-construction.
- Tri-attribute invariants: INV-A (DIVERGING iff None) covers
  auto-set on flip, auto-clear on flip, and explicit-set rejections
  in both directions; INV-B (legality per mode) covers auto-reset on
  mode change, keep-when-still-legal, and explicit-illegal
  rejection.
- Full strategy x mode legality matrix (4 modes x 7 strategies,
  legal vs illegal pairs) plus a debate-specific test verifying the
  paper-§4.3 rule that debate borrows voting and role strategies but
  not competition.
- AgenticLane: defaults, isinstance(Lane), role setter,
  trust_score validation, relaxed name (empty / spaces /
  punctuation).
- Backward compat: base Task/Gateway/Lane still importable and
  constructible, vanilla instances are not isinstance of the
  agentic subclasses.
- __repr__ for all three classes.

Full BPMN test suite passes: 119 tests = 45 pre-existing + 74 new.
Ruff clean on the CI rule set
(F841,F401,F541,F811,E711,E721,E731,E741).
